query: What distinct aspects of food quality do reviewers focus on?

per_column.name: taste_quality
per_column.rationale: Captures a distinct aspect of food quality (taste sentiment) as a groupable categorical axis, directly relevant to the query about aspects reviewers focus on. It leans toward a general sentiment flag which limits leverage somewhat, but scoping it to taste specifically adds value. Values align well with source text: positive taffy/confection, negative for medicinal soda and mislabeled peanuts. Nulls for rows not focused on taste are appropriate.

per_column.name: flavor_authenticity
per_column.rationale: Provides a genuinely distinct new axis (authenticity/naturalness of flavor) beyond raw sentiment, useful for the query. Most values are sound: 'authentic' for the artisanal confection, high null rate for silent rows is correct. However the 'Jumbo Salted Peanuts' row is about mislabeled size/salting, not artificiality of flavor, yet was tagged 'artificial_or_off'; this is a mild overreach that conflates a labeling complaint with flavor authenticity, slightly reducing groundedness.

judge.rationale: Both columns give distinct, groupable dimensions of food-quality perception (taste sentiment and flavor authenticity) that directly serve the query about aspects reviewers focus on, and they are not mere restatements of each other. Values are generally well-grounded in the source text with appropriate nulls for silent rows; the main weakness is occasional over-mapping of non-flavor complaints (mislabeling) onto flavor_authenticity.
